title: Eating for the Gym on a NZ Budget – Under $100/Week
meta_desc: Practical NZ guide to hit protein targets on a $100 weekly grocery budget. Includes cheap supermarket staples, a meal plan and prep tips for gym-goers.
intro: You don’t need pricey health foods to fuel your workouts. With a bit of planning you can meet protein goals, stay full and keep costs below $100 a week using everyday NZ supermarket items.

sections.heading: 1. Set Your Protein Target
sections.body: Research from the New Zealand Nutrition Society recommends 1.6–2.2 g of protein per kilogram of body weight for strength training. For a 75 kg (165 lb) lifter that’s 120–165 g of protein daily. Split it across meals to aid absorption and satiety.
list: Calculate your weight in kg (kg = lbs ÷ 2.2).
Multiply by 1.8 g as a middle‑ground target.
Aim for 30–40 g protein per main meal and 15–20 g in snacks.

sections.heading: 2. Shop Smart – Where and What to Buy
sections.body: Pak’nSave and Countdown’s “Everyday Value” ranges give the best price per gram of protein. Bulk packs of chicken thighs, minced beef, and canned tuna are often under $5 per kilogram. Eggs, lentils, and frozen peas are cheap, high‑protein staples. Look for store‑brand Greek yoghurt (≈$3.50 for 500 g) and milk (≈$2.30 for 2 L).
list: Canned tuna in water – $1.20 per 165 g can
Whey protein concentrate (budget brand) – $25 for 1 kg (≈25 g protein per scoop)

sections.heading: 3. Sample Weekly Meal Plan (Under $100)
sections.body: Below is a simple seven‑day plan that hits ~130 g protein daily while staying under $100 total. Adjust portion sizes if your target is higher.

rows: Grilled chicken thigh + brown rice + frozen peas
Tuna & bean salad with whole‑grain wrap

sections.heading: 4. Prep, Cook, Save Time
sections.body: Batch‑cook on Sunday to lock in protein and reduce daily cooking stress. Portion into reusable containers and refrigerate for up to four days, or freeze for longer storage. Use a large pot for lentils, a sheet pan for chicken thighs, and a slow cooker for beef mince – minimal active cooking time, maximum flavour.
list: Cook 2 kg of chicken thighs at once – 4‑5 meals ready.
Boil a 500 g bag of red lentils – use in soups, salads, or as a mince substitute.
Pre‑portion yoghurt into 150 g snack cups with a handful of berries.

sections.heading: 5. Stretch Your Budget Further
sections.body: Buy in bulk when sales run (e.g., 2 kg chicken packs for $7.80). Choose frozen veg over fresh to avoid waste. If you’re eligible for Exercise NZ’s subsidised gym scheme, you can redirect the saved money into higher‑quality protein or a basic whey supplement. Remember, consistency beats perfection – the goal is to keep protein high without breaking the bank.
